source.title: A Distributed Neural Network Training Method Based on Hybrid Gradient Computing
source.authors: Zhen-Zhou Lu; Meng Lu; Yan Liang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports ImageNet validation accuracy for optimizer comparisons and tests combinations of batch-normalization strategies that include changing single-GPU batch size.
record.gate_note: The paper reports distributed-training accuracy and speed. It does not test random-label memorization, architecture comparisons, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. The batch-size comparison is entangled with changes to batch-normalization statistics and moving-average handling.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out ImageNet accuracy across AdaBound, warmup plus SGD, and a hybrid optimizer, bearing on V4. Its precision comparison also reports unchanged validation accuracy while doubling batch size, bearing narrowly on V5's adapted-recipe clause.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their hybrid optimizer improves convergence while maintaining SGD's generalization, and that mixed precision accelerates computation and communication without accuracy loss. These are conclusions about their integrated distributed recipe.
record.recipe_differences: Distributed ImageNet ResNet-50 training with an ADABOUND warmup followed by linear-scaling SGD and LARS; it does not directly reproduce the listed optimizer or batch-size studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and warmup schedule; batch-normalization strategy, including fixed batch size, per-GPU statistics, and moving-average handling.

fits_no_version.finding: Sequential BN changes raise validation accuracy from 70.34% to 73.35%, 75.05%, and 75.60%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Keeping per-GPU batch size fixed, computing BN statistics independently per GPU, and replacing moving averages with final-iteration statistics improve accuracy in this distributed training setup.

record.peer_reviewed: Scalable Computing: Practice and Experience, Volume 21, Issue 2, pp. 323–336 (2020)
record.problems: The batch-size-related accuracy results change multiple batch-normalization settings together, so the effect of batch size cannot be isolated. The optimizer comparison reports no uncertainty estimates, and exact validation values for comparator methods are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Unmodified Adam versus SGD; systematic limited-versus-broad tuning; decoupled weight decay; language benchmarks. The hybrid changes both warmup and subsequent optimization, so switching alone is not isolated.

An unadapted large-batch penalty, a workload-dependent threshold, longer-training recovery, and a comparison against conventional small-batch training. Both batches in the precision comparison are already large.

missing.what: Record the FP32 versus mixed-precision validation comparison: global batch sizes 3072 and 6144, respectively, with almost coincident accuracy curves and greater oscillation under mixed precision. Include the shared training schedule and the simultaneous precision change.
missing.locator: Section 3.1 experimental details; Section 3.2.2, training accuracy; Figure 3.3

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Missing controls and untested tuning regimes do not themselves warrant limits_scope. The cited 64K-batch accuracy drop is prior work, not this study's result.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out performance comparison between natural and random labels.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width needed to fit.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No comparison of Adam with SGD under broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, or language-model tasks.
No isolated large-versus-small batch comparison under a fixed epoch budget, and no test of longer training or the alternative recipe adaptations named in the version.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
